newsitem.title: MEXICO: Grupo Bancomer 1996 net falls on year.
newsitem.headline: Grupo Bancomer 1996 net falls on year.

text.p: Grupo Financiero Bancomer said on Thursday its 1996 net was 448 million pesos, 11.3 percent lower than in 1995.
In a statement, the company said its 1996 fourth quarter net profit was 1.015 billion pesos compared to a 1995 fourth quarter loss of 188 million pesos.
The company said its banking subsidary showed a 1996 net profit of 170 million pesos, after extraordinary items.
Bancomer had a capitalization ratio 12.18 percent at the end of 1996, compared with 11.51 percent ratio at the end of 1995.
Before extraordinary items and a differing of tax benefits, the banking subsidiary had a net profit of 2.985 billion pesos.
The Grupo Financiero said that the rest of its subsidiaries had net profits of 264 million in 1996, compared to a net loss of 102 million pesos in 1995.
The company said it had sold 12.3 billion pesos worth of its gross mortgage portfolio to Fobaproa, the government's Bank Insurance Fund, effective December last year.
Reserves worth 4.3 billion pesos were transferred, leaving a the net portfolio sale of 8.0 billion pesos, it said.
The banking subsidiary had a gross bad loan portfolio worth 10.718 billion pesos at the end of 1996, almost 2.0 billion pesos less than during the third quarter, it said.
Reserves against the bad loan portfolio were 12.8 billion pesos, or 119 percent, compared to 85.8 percent the year before, it said.
"Our results are positive even in the light of our decision to increase our reserve coverage for bad loans in the first quarter," the company's director-general Ricardo Guajardo said in a statement.
"The non-banking subsidiaries of the Grupo made an important contribution to the results," he said.

"As well we completed with success a program of high quality capitalization for 8.0 billion pesos, and we start 1997 with the objective to strengthen our capital base, most importantly with the disinvestment of non-strategic assets," Guajardo said.
